$Comment: The introduction to the Disenchanting Table: Sawyer Marn, who already knows the player, points
them at the priest working his own corner of the Forgotten Temple. The quest exists to make
the player cross the landing and notice him.
Npc.ViewId names the sawyer's role id, so Marn is who OFFERS it: it appears on his quest list
once his own introduction is claimed, and his conversation carries a pointer line that takes
it on. The step names the enchanter's role id instead, so the errand is taken from one
character and discharged at another. Orrin's placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the
character IS the role, and any other standing of Mmo_Enchanter credits the step just as well.
TurnInAt names the enchanter, so the reward is collected where the errand ends rather than on
a walk back to the sawyer: the quest sits in the Claim bucket and waits in the log until the
player collects it from Orrin's own quest list. CompletionDialogue names Orrin's conversation,
so collecting the reward at him plays his next line, and with this introduction settled the
first job he can offer is The Lesser Table, so the player lands on the screen that hands it
over.
A talk step is credited by a MarkTalked beat inside the conversation, never by pressing F, so
Orrin's dialogue carries one on the line the player picks. Re-point the step and that beat has
to move with it.
The Enchanting experience is deliberately small: a nod toward the skill the whole table chain
trains, not a payout worth walking over for on its own. Requires.Quests names the sawyer's own
introduction, which is what chains this questline onto the end of his; the feature factor
keeps the quest out of the log on a server with the station engine switched off, where
neither character appears at all. Listing.Hidden keeps it off open listings until it is taken;
a giver always lists its own quests, so Marn still offers it.
Name: Meet_The_Enchanter
